recipes.name: Grilled Cod
ingredients_raw: 2 (8 ounce) fillets cod, cut in half
2 tablespoons chopped green onion (white part only)

steps.text: Stack about 15 charcoal briquettes into a grill in a pyramid shape. If desired, drizzle coals lightly with lighter fluid and allow to soak for 1 minute before lighting coals with a match. Allow fire to spread to all coals, about 10 minutes, before spreading briquettes out into the grill; let coals burn until a thin layer of white ash covers the coals. Lightly oil the grates.
Season both sides of cod fillets with Cajun seasoning, lemon pepper, salt, and black pepper. Set fillets aside on a plate.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, stir in lemon juice and green onion, and cook until onion is softened, about 3 minutes.
Grill cod fillets on the preheated grill until browned and flaky, about 3 minutes per side, basting frequently with butter mixture while grilling.
Allow cod to rest off the heat for about 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Cod
raw_recipe.description: Grilled cod with a Cajun spice rub is basted with lemon-butter sauce as it cooks over hot coals on the grill. Perfect for a simple but tasty summer meal.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make a grilled cod recipe for fillets basted with butter, lemon, and green onion. Serve this simple seafood dish at an outdoor dinner party, or use it in sandwiches for a quick and easy lunch.

review.reviewBody: this is a fantastic recipe. We are on a low fat, no salt diet. Used lemon-herb seasoning, more pepper & no salt. Used butter spray, not butter. Integrity of the recipe remained & we give it a 5 star pluss it's healthy.. Thanks.

Cooked this recipe as written and it was a keeper. I used Kirkland brand frozen cod and it held together nicely. I used Zatterans Creole seasoning and didn't find it to be spicy at all (eyeballing the seasoning rather than measuring), just very flavorful. I also used a stove top grill which I prefer for better control of heat. By accident I discovered a nice side dish. Boiled some new potatoes, quartered them, seasoned them, put them on the grill with the fish and basted them with the butter sauce. They're done when the fish is done.
Only comment: step one recommends using lighter fluid on charcoal. I don't recommend that. Use a charcoal chimney. If you want to cheat use a no odor fire starter.

This was, surprisingly, really good. My frozen cod fillets were a bit rubbery to start with, but I did grill them on our Jenn Aire stovetop grill and they turned out lovely (only slightly rubbery). I just sprinkled some Tony Chachere's Creole Seasoning on both sides of the fillets - no need for salt and pepper as those are the first and third ingredients, respectively, nor lemon pepper. I did melt the butter and cook some scallions in it, threw a bit of fresh lemon juice in (not an entire lemon - that would have been incredibly sour) and basted both sides of the fish once while cooking (got flare-ups from the butter hitting the gas flame). My fillets were pretty thin so I cooked 3 minutes on one side and 1 on the other. After I carefully got it off the grill (the butter pooled in the curved up fish), I poured the rest of the butter/scallion/lemon mixture on top. Very flavorful, very easy. Who would've thought?!

I changed this recipe. I used a gas grill and I did not put the cayenne pepper. I divided up 3 lbs of cod into separate portions and wrapped each piece of cod in heavy duty foil and cooked them for about 40 minutes on medium heat. The fish was cooked perfectly and I did not have the fish odor in the house for days. My son loved it.

This was fantastic ! I didn't change anything to the recipe, but I did add a few pieces of hickory to the fire for that smoked flavor. I used Riley's brand Cajun seasoning and Lawry's lemon pepper. I'll definitely be making this again!

I used frozen cod. After thawing, I dry marinated it with lemon pepper and Old Bay in the fridge for 3 hours. I breaded the fish and grilled it until just done. 
I changed the sauce. I sautéd sliced shallot in butter and then added lemon zest and juice. I finished it by whisking in Dijon mustard as an emulsion I served the sauce as a topping for the cooked fish. It turned out great.

Very tasty and so fast and easy to make! I did not alter the ingredients, my dish was seasoned perfectly. I did not broil on an outdoors grill but in my oven using the broil setting and broiler. I did not baste, just poured the butter sauce on top of the fish and cooked for 6-7 mins. Perfection!

Need to make sure your grill is good and hot. I was grilling all day, and these were the last to cook, thought my coals would last. Got a good char the grill cooled down, but finished in a 400 degree oven. Still turned out great!!

This was excellent. I took the advice of other posters and only seasoned one side, my kids are tearing it up! I used old bay seasoning, and ground pepper to season, and butter, lemon juice and a tiny bit of minced garlic to baste the cod. I also broiled it instead of grilled. Saved to make it again!

Great Cod recipe! Used Tony Chachere Creole Seasoning, lemon wedges and extra pepper (we were out of lemon pepper). Even added a little Drawn butter and renamed it....Poor Man's Lobster! Used Icelandic Cod from the fresh fish area.

It was pretty good as the contrast between the lemon pepper and the Cajun spice added depth to the flavor along with a little heat. We cooked the Cod over charcoal which really added a nice flavor. But, if we make it again I would add more spices.
Easy to follow for a none cook and dish was amazing
Why use lighter fluid it will completely ruin any BBQ cooking method. Does the person who described the the recipe ever used a a BBQ ????
Used Slap Ya Mama Cajun Seasoning....perfect.
I didn't grill outside due to bad winter weather, grilled on stovetop with butter.

excellent recipe. if you have basil growing lay a leaf on top and let it crisp. if you use a gas grill go for 460-480 degrees while cooking put place the fillets or steaks on at 475 degrees F. at any setting direct
I used Tony Chachere's as my spice and ended up with too much salt. We still ate EVERYTHING. I will use less salt next time

Loved this! I used frozen cod for this. I first soak it in lemon water, then squeeze excess water out of it with paper towels. I would season only one side next time. I also basted just once before grilling on cedar planks (gas grill)

The best grilled white fish I’ve ever made. Did not vary any ingredients or steps. I’ve prepared cod in the oven before and know when it’s done it will flake. I did put one piece of aluminum foil over grates to prevent the fish from flaking apart and falling through. I do wonder how the auto of the recipe dealt with this ? Will fix again when I can locate fresh cod, not sure how it would work out with frozen. That may explain the review that said it was rubbery. The fresher the better I believe.
